correctness.rationale: The proof reduces the weighted-forest law on any cactus to independent Bernoulli bridge/cycle blocks conditioned separately on non-full cycles. Any vertex connection factors along a unique path in the block-cut tree. For one cycle, shared-mark and noncrossing four-mark numerators factor into nonnegative terms; crossing marks admit a nonnegative 21-term degree-two Bernstein-basis certificate. The polynomial certificate is exact by 3-point interpolation in every variable, and the standalone standard-library script independently checks all identities with rational arithmetic plus finite weighted forest enumerations. This proves the all-size, all-positive-weight covariance bound; enumerations are auxiliary, not the general argument.

originality.rationale: No located source states an equivalent all-weight, all-cactus positive covariance theorem. The primary September 2026 abstract presents a high-fugacity result and a broader connectivity-correlation question, whereas the proved theorem handles arbitrary heterogeneous positive weights on every cactus graph. Equivalence to Bernoulli percolation conditioned acyclic and older edge-negative-dependence work does not itself imply the connectivity result. The full original HTML of the direct 2026 source was examined in Section 6 (Proposition 6.1 and Conjecture 6.2); an uninspected connection-focused thesis remains a specific risk; the PASS is a qualified self-review, not a uniqueness certificate.

value.rationale: Positive covariance of two vertex-pair connectivity events is a motivated conjectural direction for the arboreal gas. The theorem gives a nontrivial all-fugacity validity class (arbitrarily many cactus cycles, arbitrary nonuniform edge weights), not merely a finite enumeration or an asymptotic high-fugacity statement. The crossing configuration requires an explicit positive polynomial certificate and the block-factorization propagates the local result to an unbounded graph family. It does not purport to settle the general graph conjecture.
